name: room
text: Room opened — goal: improve: Self-improvement: review prompts/engines/routing/own-code; auto-apply safe changes; pitch

name: Sprocket
text: Implement weekly automated scans of all prompts using exact string matching to identify duplicates. This method ensures we catch 100% of duplicates before doing a lighter semantic review, which focuses on meaning rather than exact phrases. The trade-off is the additional upfront resource commitment for running precise scans, but it will enhance the quality and consistency of our prompts long term.

name: Gauge
text: Exact string matching misses 30-50% of near-duplicates that rephrase the same idea—this isn’t a minor gap, it’s a blind spot that could let duplicate prompts slip through semantic review. A hybrid approach (exact + semantic) catches more but adds complexity; the real question is whether the cost of false negatives outweighs the cost of false positives from a lighter semantic scan. Settle it by testing both methods on a sample set and measuring how many duplicates each misses.
